newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures trim losses by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures trim losses by close.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures trimmed some losses but still ended lower on Friday after falling by some five percent early in the session.
Light stop-loss selling by investment funds had contributed to the sharp falls. But traders said active price-fixing by roasters following the slide took prices back from the nadir.
New York arabica futures also came in lower on spill-over selling after Thursday's heavy fund-led long liquidation.
But the decline was slowed by further industry buying. News of widening port strike in Brazil could have provided some background support.
By the close, London's May was just $40 down at $1,570 a tonne, after recovering from a week's low of $1,515, a five-percent fall on the day.

Before the New York's sell-off, traders predicted that May could remain in the $1,610-$1,675 range for a while although they admitted that the recent wild swings had made it difficult to foretell the market direction.
Resistance is now seen at the chart gap of $1,590-$1,610 while support is seen at $1,530.
Traders noted sizeable rolling of May positions into July, which also lost $40 on the day at $1,580.
Overall volume was 6,276 lots, with May and July accounting for some 5,000 lots.
After the market had closed, private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said cooler temperaturs were heading towards Brazil's coffee belt next week, but there was no threat of frost.

While the weather would be unusually cool for this time of the year, temperatures in Brazil's coffee areas were only expected to drop into the lows 50s Fahrenheit (low teens C). It need temperatures in the mid-30s to get frost.
Two severe frosts in 1994, one in late June and another in early July, damaged Brazilian crop. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
